clips.text: Connect the anatomy to vocabulary. Stenosis is narrowing that obstructs forward flow. Regurgitation is backward leakage. Atresia is an absent or closed normal opening. Cardiomyopathy affects heart muscle. Heart failure is a clinical syndrome caused by impaired cardiac filling or pumping, which can produce congestion, inadequate circulation, or both. It can occur with reduced or preserved ejection fraction; a normal ejection fraction alone does not diagnose a filling problem or exclude heart failure.

clips.text: Pericarditis affects the sac around the heart. Myocarditis affects the heart muscle. Endocarditis often involves infection of the endocardial surface, especially valves, although noninfectious forms exist. Ischemia means inadequate blood supply relative to tissue needs; infarction means tissue death caused by prolonged inadequate supply. Adult heart muscle has limited regenerative capacity, and significant injury often leaves scar. Avoid the absolute claim that no cardiac cell can ever renew.

clips.text: Atherosclerosis is a complex inflammatory plaque process involving lipids, cells, fibrous tissue, and sometimes calcium in artery walls. Plaque can narrow a vessel; disruption can trigger local clot formation and acute loss of flow. Arteriosclerosis is the broader term for arterial thickening and stiffening. H D L and L D L are lipoproteins, not simply good and bad fats. Tissue injury depends on blood supply, demand, duration, and collateral flow, not a claim that everything below one clot immediately dies.

clips.text: Sympathetic activity generally increases heart rate, conduction, and contractile force. Parasympathetic activity through the vagus mainly slows sinus rate and A V nodal conduction. Vascular responses depend on receptor type and tissue; sympathetic activity does not simply dilate every vessel, and parasympathetic activity does not universally constrict them. Hormones also affect circulation: vasopressin promotes water retention, aldosterone promotes sodium retention, and atrial natriuretic peptide promotes sodium and water excretion.

clips.text: Some medicines change heart rate, conduction, ion currents, or contractile force. Examples include beta blockers, selected calcium-channel blockers, antiarrhythmic drugs, and digoxin. Their effects differ by drug and tissue, so a class label is not a complete prediction of a tracing. Digoxin inhibits the sodium-potassium pump, indirectly affecting calcium handling. This is mechanism vocabulary for study, not guidance to start, stop, select, or dose a medication.

clips.text: E C G and E K G name the same type of recording. The electrocardiograph is the instrument; the electrocardiogram is the recording. Augustus Waller published a human electrocardiogram in eighteen eighty-seven. Willem Einthoven developed the string-galvanometer method in the early nineteen hundreds and received the nineteen twenty-four Nobel Prize. Monitoring work requires careful observation, communication, and facility-specific training. Workload, pay, shifts, and certification requirements vary, so the source's examples are not universal facts.

clips.text: Heart-disease risk reflects both nonmodifiable factors, such as age and inherited background, and modifiable factors, such as smoking, blood pressure, cholesterol, and activity patterns. Conditions can have overlapping symptoms, including breathlessness, fatigue, swelling, palpitations, or chest discomfort. A symptom list does not identify one disease or prove that a rhythm is its cause. In this lesson, connect the vocabulary to anatomy and function without making a diagnosis from a model, a strip, or a checklist.
